skill.displayName: 睿观-图片政策合规监测

llm.summary: The skill performs the advertised image compliance check, but it also includes account login, API-key generation, billing, public image upload, and local response storage that need careful review before use.

dimensions.detail: Network calls to LinkFox are expected for this service, but sensitive endpoints are configurable through environment variables and can carry API keys, access tokens, phone login data, images, and billing requests.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: There is no install-time execution or background setup in the inspected artifacts; behavior is exposed through Python scripts invoked by the agent.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill documents auth/billing fallbacks, local-image upload, response persistence, and automatic feedback reporting, but consent and scoping are weak for local image publication, phone/OTP handling, API-key output, and sending feedback content to an external API.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The search script writes full responses and cache files locally by default and may fall back to home or temporary directories despite the skill text saying current-directory storage and no /tmp; the onboarding flow also prints raw API keys to stdout.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core Ruiguan image similarity search matches the stated purpose, but the bundled onboarding CLI can collect phone/SMS login codes, obtain or generate API keys, list plans, create payment orders, and render payment QR codes; these support paid API access but materially exceed the frontmatter's image-compliance positioning.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending product image URLs, and possibly local images, phone numbers, SMS codes, API keys, feedback content, and billing requests to LinkFox services. Prefer creating or retrieving API keys directly on the official LinkFox site, verify gateway environment variables before use, avoid uploading confidential images, and delete local linkfox response/cache files when no longer needed.
llm.findings:
[TT3] unexpected: Confirmed: onboarding.py builds login, agent-user, and gateway destinations from environment-controlled base URLs while sending authentication material. Default hosts are LinkFox, so this is not evidence of malicious exfiltration by itself, but it is a real credential-routing concern.
[LP3] unexpected: Confirmed in substance: network, environment, upload, credential, billing, and file-write behavior are spread across docs and scripts without a concise permission/consent boundary.
[TP4] unexpected: Partly confirmed and downgraded from deceptive to Review concern: auth and billing are documented as fallback support flows, but they are high-impact capabilities beyond the narrow image-checking purpose.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Confirmed for onboarding.py and references/onboarding.md: phone/SMS login, API-key retrieval, plan listing, and billing support are broader than the declared image-compliance function.
[SDI-1] expected: The search script's local caching and full-response storage are explicitly documented and tied to cost control and later inspection, but retaining full payloads by default is still overbroad.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Confirmed: the skill can create payment orders and payment QR outputs. The docs require plan and method selection and say not to poll automatically, so this is not automatic unauthorized purchase behavior, but it is high-impact authority.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Confirmed: ruiguan_image_compliance_search.py says current-directory storage and no /tmp in documentation, while implementation can fall back to ~/linkfox or the system temp directory.
[SQP-1] expected: The activation wording is broad but still centered on image-based product compliance; the concern is mainly that broad triggering combines with upload, cost, and persistence behavior.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Confirmed across local upload, onboarding, API docs, and stdout behavior: local files become public URLs, phone/OTP flows are mediated by the script, image URLs and feedback content are sent externally, and API keys can be printed without strong user-facing safeguards.
[SSD-3] expected: Confirmed: full API responses are saved by default and small responses are printed. This is disclosed in SKILL.md, but it increases local and transcript exposure.
[E1] expected: External transmission is necessary for the hosted compliance service, but the sensitive onboarding and token flows make endpoint validation and user consent more important.
